The response provides a comprehensive and accurate overview of key Japanese business etiquette norms. It covers the most critical areas—greetings, business cards, dress, punctuality, address, communication style, dining, gift-giving, physical contact, and discretion—with specific, actionable details (e.g., 15-degree bow, bilingual cards presented with two hands, odd-numbered gifts). The advice is culturally sound, well-organized, and immediately useful for someone preparing for business interactions in Japan. Minor nuances (e.g., bowing depth varies by context; finishing food vs. leaving some) could be added for depth, but the response is already highly effective as a practical guide.
